working_definition: Most advanced primary spermatocyte state in the adult testis, before the meiotic divisions; manual annotation (no authors' FBbt id).

best_match.fbbt_definition: Male germ cells of the 16-cell cyst from the end of the S-phase that precedes meiosis I to the end of meiosis I. This S-phase occurs very early in the 16-cell cyst stage so almost all 16 cell cysts are at the primary spermatocyte stage.

justification: The label names primary spermatocyte with a 'late' stage qualifier. FBbt has 'mature primary spermatocyte' (morphological late, fully grown stage), but the authors' 'late' is a transcriptional cluster state, so equivalence is not assumed; primary spermatocyte is the type named.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Late, fully grown primary spermatocyte with a large central nucleus, blocky in appearance, often with indentations or grooves, containing Y-loops and a prominent nucleolus. The second nuclear membrane is fully formed. It has a highly developed endoplasmic reticulum, with mitochondria between the cisternae.
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Morphology-defined stage; equivalence to the authors' late cluster not established.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Male germline cell that is part of the 16-cell spermatocyte cyst. It expresses twine, which regulates the meiotic cycle (Witt et al., 2019).
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Less specific than the primary spermatocyte named in the label.

recommendation: Use primary spermatocyte (broad); curator may prefer mature primary spermatocyte.
